newsitem.title: UK: Science finds another good reason to hate spiders.
newsitem.headline: Science finds another good reason to hate spiders.

text.p: Tarantulas are frightening for a good reason but it is not their venom -- it's their hairy legs, British doctors said on Tuesday. The spiders flick barbed hairs from their bodies, which get into people's eyes and cause severe damage, Dr Jeremy Hung and colleagues at Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool said.
Hung described the case of a nine-year-old boy who had inflamed and swollen eyes. It turned out he had spider hairs embedded in them, and required four months of steroid treatment.

"Contrary to popular belief, (tarantula) venom is generally not very harmful, and bites caused by them are usually not much worse than wasp bites," Hung wrote in a letter to medical journal Archives of Disease in Childhood.
"However, when these animals feel threatened, they quickly flick off clouds of abdominal hairs with their legs."
The hairs were irritating and could be impossible to remove. "It actually kills small animals if they inhale it," Hung said.
Hung said the problem would grow as tarantulas became fashionable pets and any species could be dangerous.
Red-kneed Mexican tarantulas are especially popular as they are docile. It was a red-kneed spider that the nine-year-old child had.
"I have seen the actual beast that caused the problem," Hung said. He recommended that people should wear gloves and goggles when handling the spiders.
